summary: Frontend-only verification of the user auth bug fix (localStorage app). All 4 scenarios in the review request passed: (1) create user rajesh/test1234 -> login -> save vendor (Temp Ref ID generated) -> simulate logout -> re-login SUCCEEDED (the original reported bug is fixed); (2) whitespace defense — trailing spaces trimmed on both create and login, clean creds worked; (3) admin/admin@123 regression still works; (4) duplicate username blocked with 'Username already exists' toast. Prefill of username on tab-switch after create also verified.
critical_code_review_comments: Login error message leaks the full registered usernames list to the UI (Login.jsx line ~28). This is a minor security/UX smell — consider showing only a generic message; listing usernames could aid credential enumeration if this app ever gets multi-user access.
Password stored in plaintext in localStorage (acceptable given stated scope as a local-only prototype, but worth flagging if this ever moves to a shared context).
test_credentials: admin/admin@123 (seeded). Test users created during run: rajesh/test1234, priya/pass1234.
seed_data_creation: None persisted — localStorage.clear() called before each scenario.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth bug fix verified end-to-end. Trim() applied consistently in createUser() and login() in store.js works correctly. Do not need to retest this flow unless auth code changes.
rca of the issue: Original bug: password stored with trailing whitespace (from create form) while login compared against user-typed no-whitespace version, causing 'Invalid credentials'. Fix in /app/frontend/src/lib/store.js: createUser trims password before storage (line 340), login trims both username and password before comparison (lines 370-371); Login.jsx submitCreate also trims before calling createUser. Verified: user 'priya ' with password 'pass1234 ' (trailing spaces) is stored as 'priya'/'pass1234' and login with clean 'priya'/'pass1234' succeeds.
